listings.name: Hunting and fishing license fee waiver for active-duty Michiganders
listings.summary: License fees are waived for full-time active-duty service members who keep Michigan residency, except hunting licenses won through a drawing.
listings.eligibility: Full-time active-duty federal military member who has maintained Michigan residency.
listings.how_to_apply: Show military ID, leave or duty papers, or orders plus a Michigan driver's license or voter registration card when getting licenses.

listings.name: CDL skills test waiver for military drivers
listings.organization: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
listings.summary: Waives certain commercial driver's license tests for service members and veterans based on their military commercial-vehicle training and experience.
listings.eligibility: Service members and veterans with qualifying military truck or heavy-vehicle driving experience, as set out on the state's military waiver application.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the Michigan Application for Military Waiver / Even Exchange (PDF) and submit it as the form directs.
listings.notes: The application form itself was not read; check it for the time limit after separation.

listings.name: Children of Veterans Tuition Grant
listings.organization: MI Student Aid (Michigan Department of Treasury)
listings.summary: Up to $2,800 a year ($1,400 a semester full-time) toward undergraduate tuition, for up to four years or $11,200, for children of Michigan veterans who died or became totally and permanently disabled from service, or are missing in action.
listings.eligibility: Parent was a Michigan resident before entering service (or became one after) and was killed in action or died during a war or war condition, died or became totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected condition (per VA), or is MIA in a foreign country. Student is the natural or adopted child, older than 16 and younger than 26, an undergraduate at least half-time at a participating Michigan college, with a 2.25 cumulative GPA, 12 months of Michigan residency, a high school diploma or equivalent, and a FAFSA filed each year.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the MiSSG Student Portal linked from the program page and upload your birth certificate (naming the veteran), the veteran's DD-214, and proof of the veteran's death or total and permanent disability. File the FAFSA every year.
listings.deadline: 2026-27 school year: June 30, 2027; 2027-28 school year: June 30, 2028
listings.location: Participating Michigan public and private nonprofit colleges
listings.source_title: Children of Veterans Tuition Grant (MI Student Aid)
listings.notes: Future awards depend on available funding. No counts of awards published on the page.

listings.name: County veteran burial payment
listings.summary: A $300 burial expense payment from the county for an eligible veteran, spouse or surviving spouse.
listings.eligibility: Eligible deceased veterans, their spouses or surviving spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: Ask your county veteran affairs office or an accredited Veteran Service Officer (1-800-MICH-VET or the MVAA county locator) how to file.
listings.notes: Stated on MVAA's benefits page; MVAA's burial page covers federal burial benefits and does not detail the county payment or its deadline.

listings.name: Task Force 1620 veteran cannabis access programs
listings.summary: Licensed Michigan cannabis businesses in the CRA's Task Force 1620 run veteran access programs offering cannabis at a 75% to 100% discount.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who meet the participating retailer's own criteria, which can include a minimum disability rating; each retailer sets its limits.
listings.how_to_apply: Check the CRA's list of Task Force 1620 retailers and ask the retailer about its veteran program.
listings.notes: Licensed businesses join with the TF1620 form; questions CRA-SocialEquity@michigan.gov.

listings.name: Veteran Recognition Program for veteran-owned cannabis businesses
listings.summary: Majority veteran-owned licensed cannabis businesses get a CRA recognition letter and seal and are listed by name and license number on the CRA website.
listings.eligibility: Cannabis business licensed under the MMFLA or MRTMA that is majority-owned by U.S. armed forces veterans, based on the ownership structure on file with the CRA.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the Veteran Recognition Program form (PDF) from the CRA page; a 2026 renewal form is posted for current participants.
listings.source_title: Veteran Recognition Program (Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency)
listings.notes: No fee reduction is mentioned. Questions: CRA-SocialEquity@michigan.gov.

listings.name: Disabled Veterans Exemption (homestead property tax)
listings.summary: Full property tax exemption on the primary residence (homestead) of an eligible disabled veteran or un-remarried surviving spouse, under MCL 211.7b.
listings.eligibility: Disabled veteran discharged from the U.S. armed forces under honorable conditions who owns and lives in the home, or that veteran's un-remarried surviving spouse. The Treasury page read does not spell out the disability rating required.
listings.how_to_apply: The Treasury page read does not list the form or filing steps; ask your city or township assessor, or a Veteran Service Officer through 1-800-MICH-VET.
listings.source_title: Disabled Veterans Exemption (Michigan Department of Treasury)
listings.notes: MVAA's benefits page calls it a full exemption on a primary residence. Treasury links a 'Disabled Veterans Exemption Information' page that was not read; check it for the rating requirement, form and deadline.

listings.name: Ex-Prisoner of War license plate
listings.organization: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
listings.summary: A reduced-cost license plate for former prisoners of war, available regardless of disability rating; spouses are eligible.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who were prisoners of war, and their spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: Order by mail with the Application for Veteran License Plate (BDVR-87).
listings.notes: Holders also qualify for free state park entry with the plate.

listings.name: Fireworks Free Fourth of July camping
listings.summary: Select state park campgrounds farther from community fireworks are set aside as quieter, fireworks-free camping over the Fourth of July weekend for veterans and others who want a calmer holiday.
listings.eligibility: Open to veterans and any camper wanting a quieter Fourth of July.
listings.how_to_apply: Reserve a site at a participating state park campground through Michigan State Parks.
listings.deadline: Fourth of July weekend each year; 2027 participating campgrounds not yet published

listings.name: Free hunting and fishing licenses for disabled veterans
listings.summary: Free hunting and fishing licenses (those that do not require a separate drawing application) for Michigan resident veterans who are 100% permanently and totally disabled or individually unemployable.
listings.eligibility: Michigan resident veteran whom the VA has rated permanently and totally disabled from military service and entitled to benefits at the 100% rate (not for blindness), or rated individually unemployable.
listings.how_to_apply: Get licenses through the DNR license system or a license agent, showing VA documentation of your status; carry it while hunting or fishing.
listings.deadline: License season: fishing licenses run March 1 to March 31 of the following year
listings.notes: Fees are not waived for nonresidents.

listings.name: Free Recreation Passport entry to state parks
listings.summary: Free entry to Michigan state parks and other sites that require a Recreation Passport for Medal of Honor recipients, 100% disabled veterans and former prisoners of war.
listings.eligibility: Medal of Honor recipients, veterans rated 100% disabled, and ex-prisoners of war, who must have the matching specialty license plate designation.
listings.how_to_apply: Have the qualifying specialty plate on your vehicle; see the DNR Recreation Passport page.

listings.name: Free financial counseling through GreenPath (MVTF partner)
listings.organization: GreenPath Financial Wellness, partner of the Michigan Veterans Trust Fund
listings.summary: Free financial counseling for veterans through a nonprofit partner of the Michigan Veterans Trust Fund.
listings.eligibility: Veterans; MVAA describes the counseling as free to veterans.
listings.how_to_apply: Call GreenPath at 800-550-1961 or start on its military service page.

listings.name: High school diplomas for wartime veterans
listings.summary: Wartime veterans who left high school early to serve can be awarded a high school diploma.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who served during wartime and left high school before graduating to serve.
listings.how_to_apply: MVAA lists the benefit without an application link; call 1-800-MICH-VET or ask a Veteran Service Officer how to request it.

listings.name: HUD-VASH housing vouchers (MSHDA)
listings.organization: Michigan State Housing Development Authority (MSHDA) with the VA
listings.summary: Rental vouchers for homeless veterans paired with VA case management; the family pays no more than 40% of income toward rent and the voucher pays the rest to the landlord.
listings.eligibility: Homeless veterans and their families who take part in VA case management.
listings.how_to_apply: You cannot apply online. Contact your local VA case manager, who refers eligible families to the housing authority. VA centers assigned to MSHDA: Lansing VA Clinic 517-267-3925, Detroit VAMC 313-576-1000, Saginaw VAMC 989-497-2500, Iron Mountain VAMC 906-774-3300.
listings.source_title: HUD VASH (Veterans Administration Supportive Housing) Vouchers
listings.notes: Federal HUD-VA program administered in Michigan by MSHDA and other housing authorities; voucher counts are not published on the page.

listings.name: In-state tuition for veterans and service members
listings.summary: Veterans and active-duty service members qualify for in-state tuition in Michigan regardless of their residency or duty status.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and active-duty service members, regardless of state residency.
listings.how_to_apply: Tell the admissions or veterans office at the Michigan public college or university; MVAA lists this benefit without a separate application link.
listings.notes: Useful for Ohio veterans attending school in Michigan. MVAA gives no statute or link; confirm with the school.

listings.name: Michigan Incarcerated Veterans' In-Reach Program (MIVIP)
listings.organization: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (LEO)
listings.summary: Pre-release education, employment-readiness training and career guidance for incarcerated veterans, with wraparound support after release.
listings.eligibility: Veterans incarcerated at seven Michigan facilities: Carson City, Cooper Street, G. Robert Cotton, Women's Huron Valley, Parnall, Saginaw and St. Louis correctional facilities.
listings.how_to_apply: Ask facility staff about MIVIP, or email the Veterans' Employment Services team at veteransservices@michigan.gov.
listings.notes: Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor Pathway Home 3 grant.

listings.name: Professional licensing help and fee waivers for veterans (LARA)
listings.organization: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA)
listings.summary: Military training and experience can count toward Michigan occupational and professional licenses, with initial and renewal fee waivers for veterans; LARA lists licensing resources for nearly 90 health, occupational and skilled-trade licenses.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members entering a regulated profession; specific waiver rules vary by license.
listings.how_to_apply: Start on LARA's Licensing Resources for Veterans page and follow the link for your license type.
listings.notes: The fee waiver and experience credit are stated on MVAA's benefits page; LARA's own veterans page lists license resources but does not spell out waiver rules.

listings.name: Educator certification guidance for service members and veterans
listings.summary: Michigan Department of Education guidance and supports for veterans and service members pursuing careers in public schools.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members seeking Michigan educator certification.
listings.how_to_apply: See the Department of Education's military guidance page for certification steps.

listings.name: Michigan Veteran Connector network
listings.summary: A statewide network of health systems, businesses and community members who commit to asking 'Have you served?' and steering veterans to MVAA's Benefits Checkup; MVAA gives connectors a toolkit.
listings.eligibility: Organizations and community members, including veterans, who want to help other veterans find benefits.
listings.how_to_apply: Email mvaastrategy@michigan.gov to become a connector.

listings.name: Income tax exemption for military pay, retirement and pensions
listings.summary: Active-duty and retired military pay and military pensions are exempt from Michigan individual income tax, and military disability retirement pay is not counted as taxable income.
listings.eligibility: Current and retired members of the U.S. armed forces with Michigan income tax filing requirements.
listings.how_to_apply: Claimed on your Michigan income tax return; the pages read describe no separate application.
listings.deadline: With your annual Michigan income tax return
listings.notes: Treasury's pension page confirms 'Military pensions, Social Security & Railroad benefits continue to be exempt from tax.'

listings.name: Military and veteran license plates
listings.organization: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
listings.summary: Specialty plates for branch veterans, Guard and Reserve, Merchant Marine, Blue Star and Gold Star families, Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, women veterans, conflict and era service, and disabled veterans rated 50% to 90%.
listings.eligibility: Depends on the plate: honorable discharge or retirement for branch plates; current or former members for Guard and Reserve; documented service dates for conflict plates; family members for Blue Star and Gold Star plates.
listings.how_to_apply: Order new plates by mail with the Application for Veteran License Plate (BDVR-87). Replacement plates can be ordered online at renewal.
listings.cost: Fees not listed on the page
listings.source_title: Military and veteran plate options (Michigan SOS)

listings.name: 1-800-MICH-VET Resource Service Center and Benefits Checkup
listings.summary: MVAA's statewide line for free help: schedule a Benefits Checkup, get referred to an accredited county Veteran Service Officer, and get help with housing instability or emergencies.
listings.eligibility: Michigan veterans and their families.
listings.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-MICH-VET (800-642-4838) or email MVAAResourceCenter@michigan.gov; find a VSO with MVAA's county locator.
listings.location: By phone; VSOs in every region
listings.notes: MVAA states its services are free.

listings.name: Michigan National Guard State Tuition Assistance Program (MINGSTAP)
listings.organization: Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
listings.summary: State tuition assistance for Michigan National Guard members at Michigan colleges, trade and technical schools: up to $14,400 for an associate or bachelor's degree and up to $6,000 for training, certificate or master's programs; spouses and dependent children can use the member's benefit.
listings.eligibility: Active member of the Michigan National Guard in good standing (not AWOL or facing MCMJ/UCMJ charges) who meets any added criteria set by the Adjutant General. Under Public Act 33 of 2023, a member's spouse, or dependent child, stepchild or adopted child who has finished high school or turned 18 and uses it before age 26, may use the member's benefit.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the MINGSTAP application linked on the DMVA page for the term you plan to attend; reimbursements run through a SIGMA vendor account.
listings.deadline: Apply each term; no specific dates published
listings.location: Michigan colleges, universities, trade and technical schools
listings.notes: For current Guard members and their families, not separated veterans. Email MINGSTAP@michigan.gov; online office hours Tue 10-11 a.m., Wed noon-1 p.m., Thu 3-4 p.m.

listings.name: Michigan Operation Freedom Outdoors (MiOFO)
listings.summary: Outdoor recreation for wounded veterans and people with health challenges, centered on the DNR's Sharonville State Game Area and neighboring Camp Liberty, building a support network for recovery through nature.
listings.eligibility: Wounded veterans and people with health challenges.
listings.how_to_apply: See MiOFO's website for events and sign-up.
listings.location: Sharonville State Game Area and Camp Liberty, southern Michigan
listings.notes: Partnership of the DNR with Camp Liberty, Brain Injury Association, DAV, American Legion and others; event schedule not on the MVAA page.

listings.name: Free permanent Disabled Veteran license plate
listings.organization: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
listings.summary: One free permanent plate for a private passenger vehicle that never needs tabs, for totally or permanently disabled veterans; a surviving spouse can transfer it when the title transfers.
listings.eligibility: Veteran with a total or permanent and total disability rating and an honorable discharge.
listings.how_to_apply: Order by mail with the Application for Veteran License Plate (BDVR-87). A disability parking placard is still needed for disability spaces.
listings.source_title: Military and veteran plate options (Michigan SOS)
listings.notes: MVAA's benefits page calls this plate free; the SOS page does not list a fee.

listings.name: Veterans' preference for State of Michigan civil service jobs
listings.summary: Eligible veterans and certain spouses get preference when applying for initial State of Michigan civil service jobs.
listings.eligibility: Veteran with 90+ days of active duty and an honorable discharge (or within six months of an expected honorable discharge), a disabled veteran eligible for VA service-connected compensation, a surviving spouse of a veteran, a spouse of a veteran rated more than 50% service-connected, or a surviving spouse with a child under 18 or caring for a disabled child. Must meet the job's minimum qualifications.
listings.how_to_apply: Register with the Michigan Civil Service Commission when applying for state jobs and document your eligibility (DD-214; VA letter for disability).
listings.source_title: Qualifying for Veterans' Preference (Civil Service Commission Rule 3-8, revised 09/05/2021)
listings.notes: The rule does not state point values. Questions: MCSC-Compensation@michigan.gov.

listings.name: Unemployment insurance for former military members (UCX)
listings.summary: Unemployment benefits for recently separated service members, with a 24/7 hotline and a brochure for veterans with unemployment questions.
listings.eligibility: Former military service members who are unemployed after separation (UCX rules apply).
listings.how_to_apply: File a claim with the Unemployment Insurance Agency; for claim-filing help call 866-500-0017, or use the 24/7 hotline 855-707-8387.

listings.name: Veteran-Friendly Employer program
listings.summary: MVAA recognizes Michigan employers with strong veteran hiring and retention practices; veterans can target recognized employers, and employers can apply for recognition.
listings.eligibility: Michigan employers apply; any veteran job seeker can use the recognition to find veteran-friendly workplaces.
listings.how_to_apply: Employers apply through MVAA's Veteran-Friendly Employer page.

listings.name: Veteran-Friendly School program
listings.summary: MVAA recognizes Michigan colleges and training schools that serve student veterans well; the dashboard helps veterans pick a school with strong veteran support.
listings.eligibility: Any veteran or military-connected student choosing a school; schools apply for recognition.
listings.how_to_apply: Browse the Veteran-Friendly School dashboard on MVAA's site.
listings.notes: Dashboard page itself was not read; counts of recognized schools not recorded.

listings.name: Michigan Veteran Homelessness Prevention Grant (MiVHPG)
listings.summary: State funding for Michigan nonprofits that give veterans emergency shelter (including hotel stays), affordable housing, family support such as financial aid, counseling and child care, and landlord incentives. Veterans facing homelessness can call 1-800-MICH-VET for help.
listings.eligibility: Michigan-based nonprofit organizations apply for funding; veterans who are homeless or at risk get help through funded programs and MVAA's hotline.
listings.how_to_apply: Organizations: see the Notice of Funding Opportunity linked on MVAA's Veteran Homelessness page. Veterans: call 1-800-MICH-VET or email MVAAResourceCenter@michigan.gov.
listings.notes: Grant cycle dates, amounts and grantee counts were not published on the page read.

listings.name: Michigan Veteran Homes at Chesterfield Township
listings.organization: Michigan Veteran Homes (Michigan Veterans Affairs Agency)
listings.summary: State veterans home offering skilled nursing, long-term care, dementia and memory care, and palliative care in a home-like setting.
listings.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is eligible for VA health care or VA financial help for long-term nursing care, or a dependent of an eligible veteran (spouse, widow or widower, former spouse, or Gold Star parent). Michigan residency is not required.
listings.how_to_apply: Start on the Michigan Veteran Homes 'Apply for Admission' page; a Veteran Service Officer (1-800-MICH-VET) can help with VA eligibility paperwork.
listings.cost: Not published on the pages read; MVH refers to its VA benefits and cost-of-care page (https://www.michigan.gov/mvh/eligibility/va-benefits)

capacity.slots: 128 members, each with a private bedroom and bathroom, in four 32-member neighborhood buildings
capacity.figure_date: As published on the home's page, Nov 2026

listings.source_title: Michigan Veteran Homes at Chesterfield Township (Michigan Veteran Homes)
listings.notes: Michigan residency is not required, so out-of-state veterans (including Ohio veterans) may apply. Also offers short-term rehab and therapy, in-house pharmacy and dental and vision clinics. No waitlist figures published. Eligibility from https://www.michigan.gov/mvh/eligibility.

listings.name: Michigan Veteran Homes D.J. Jacobetti
listings.organization: Michigan Veteran Homes (Michigan Veterans Affairs Agency)
listings.summary: State veterans home offering skilled nursing, long-term care, dementia and memory care, and palliative care in a home-like setting.
listings.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is eligible for VA health care or VA financial help for long-term nursing care, or a dependent of an eligible veteran (spouse, widow or widower, former spouse, or Gold Star parent). Michigan residency is not required.
listings.how_to_apply: Start on the Michigan Veteran Homes 'Apply for Admission' page; a Veteran Service Officer (1-800-MICH-VET) can help with VA eligibility paperwork.
listings.cost: Not published on the pages read; MVH refers to its VA benefits and cost-of-care page (https://www.michigan.gov/mvh/eligibility/va-benefits)

capacity.slots: Maximum member census of 126 at the current home; a replacement home for 108 members in private rooms is under construction in Marquette Township
capacity.figure_date: As published on the home's page, Nov 2026

listings.source_title: Michigan Veteran Homes D.J. Jacobetti (Michigan Veteran Homes)
listings.notes: Michigan residency is not required, so out-of-state veterans (including Ohio veterans) may apply. Admissions line 906-225-6889. Replacement home broke ground May 23, 2025; no opening date published (page estimates 30-36 months of construction, then phased move-in). No waitlist figures published. Eligibility from https://www.michigan.gov/mvh/eligibility.

listings.name: Michigan Veteran Homes at Grand Rapids
listings.organization: Michigan Veteran Homes (Michigan Veterans Affairs Agency)
listings.summary: State veterans home offering skilled nursing, long-term care, dementia and memory care, and palliative care in a home-like setting.
listings.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is eligible for VA health care or VA financial help for long-term nursing care, or a dependent of an eligible veteran (spouse, widow or widower, former spouse, or Gold Star parent). Michigan residency is not required.
listings.how_to_apply: Start on the Michigan Veteran Homes 'Apply for Admission' page; a Veteran Service Officer (1-800-MICH-VET) can help with VA eligibility paperwork.
listings.location: 2950 Monroe Avenue NE, Grand Rapids, MI 49505
listings.cost: Not published on the pages read; MVH refers to its VA benefits and cost-of-care page (https://www.michigan.gov/mvh/eligibility/va-benefits)

capacity.slots: 128 members, each with a private bedroom and bathroom, in four 32-member neighborhood buildings
capacity.figure_date: As published on the home's page, Nov 2026

listings.source_title: Michigan Veteran Homes at Grand Rapids (Michigan Veteran Homes)
listings.notes: Michigan residency is not required, so out-of-state veterans (including Ohio veterans) may apply. Also offers short-term rehab and therapy, a psychiatric program, in-house pharmacy and dental and vision clinics. No waitlist figures published. Eligibility from https://www.michigan.gov/mvh/eligibility.

listings.name: Veterans' Employment Services at Michigan Works!
listings.organization: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (LEO)
listings.summary: One-on-one career services for veterans and eligible spouses at Michigan Works! centers, with priority of service, veteran career advisors and help connecting with employers.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with at least one day of active military service and eligible spouses qualify for priority of service; intensive services focus on veterans facing barriers to employment.
listings.how_to_apply: Call 800-285-9675 (800-285-WORKS) or visit a Michigan Works! service center and tell staff you are a veteran or eligible spouse.

listings.name: Michigan Veterans Trust Fund Emergency Grant Program
listings.summary: Discretionary grants for a temporary or short-term financial emergency or hardship; the fund has paid utility bills, home repairs and mortgage help. A 65+ Peacetime Program covers older peacetime-era veterans.
listings.eligibility: Honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge, plus 180 days of active duty during a period of war (or with an Armed Forces or Marine Corps Expeditionary Medal), or at least one day of wartime service with separation for a line-of-duty disability. Peacetime-era veterans with 180 days of service can apply any time during the year they turn 65. Dependents of an eligible veteran may apply in some cases.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the MVTF county committee for the county where you live (county guide on the MVTF page) or with help from a local accredited Veteran Service Officer. Bring your DD-214, proof of residence, the bills you need help with, any disability rating, and proof of income.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time (65+ Peacetime Program: during the year you turn 65)

capacity.served: 557 emergency grants approved (517 in full, 40 in part), $2,017,443 paid, in FY2025
capacity.applicants: 911 applications in FY2025 (156 disapproved, 19 ineligible, 182 withdrawn)

odds.text: 557 of 911 applications were approved in full or in part in FY2025: about 61%. 182 were withdrawn.

listings.notes: No fixed grant limit is published; the FY2025 report gives an average approved grant of $3,622 and says the Board has approved some applications over $20,000. The 65+ Peacetime Program paid $204,940.97 in FY2025. Denials can be appealed to the MVTF Board at its monthly meeting.
